commits.message:
feat(docs): a simulated process runs an example's own new Console() in a terminal we supply (rich-docs-examples-xuu.iy5)

`runInTerminal(program, terminal)` evaluates a bundled program as the body of
an async function whose parameter is named `process`, so every free `process`
in it — the library included — binds to a stand-in built from the terminal.
Nothing global is swapped: the build's and the page's own `process` are never
touched, and two runs can overlap.

Proven in Node (test/docs/simulated-process.test.ts, under a hostile host env)
and in Chromium (e2e/simulated-process.spec.ts).

fix(live): alt-screen rows are erased before drawing, not padded to a width

Review of #163: padding each row to options.maxWidth threw on an unbounded
console width (' '.repeat(Infinity)), and parsing the width would not have
helped — Infinity is a cell count. Erasing the row first clears the last
frame's cells with no width at all, from column 0 where the erase is safe.

The Height contract said an inline Live crops taller output; it applies its
verticalOverflow, and 'visible' scrolls.

fix(live): an alt-screen frame writes every cell, and a transient stop erases nothing

Review of #163: the alternate screen is only homed between frames, so a
shorter frame left the last one's rows and line tails showing. Its rows are
now padded to the width. Its lines are no longer counted for _clearLast,
which was one row off now the cursor ends on the last row, and pointless
before leaving the buffer.

Console.options reads the size once, and Live takes its rows from those
options. print's stackedHeight was an identity on a ceiling, so it is gone.
The Height contract says what the setter of a ceiling does with taller
output: Live crops it, print lets it scroll. The inline full-height scroll
is rich-live-4rh.

feat(render): Console and Live supply the Height budget (rich-viewport-owi.2)

Console.options carries the terminal's rows as a ceiling, and print hands
each stacked block stackedHeight of it. Live renders under the same rows:
inline as a ceiling with its crop kept, alt-screen as a region shaped with
fitHeight and written with no newline after the last row, so a full-height
frame no longer scrolls.

insetHeight, stackedHeight, regionRows and fitHeight are exported from the
barrel and documented in docs/protocol.md beside the width contract.

rich-dash's InjectMaxHeight wrapper and its reserved row are gone: Live
supplies the height they injected. The job pane gains a build-log tail that
fills the rows under its bars, which is what demonstrates the four helpers.

docs/live.md dropped a false claim that the last frame is shown `visible`
on stop — stop() refreshes under the configured overflow.

refactor(protocol)!: one Height budget replaces height and maxHeight (rich-viewport-owi.1) (#162)

* refactor(protocol)!: one Height budget replaces height and maxHeight (rich-viewport-owi.1)

RenderOptions carried a vertical budget as two independent optional numbers,
which admitted a region taller than its ceiling and a region with no ceiling,
and the one reader (Layout) resolved them ceiling-first. It is now one field,
`height?: Height` — `{ rows, exact }` — whose doc comment is the contract:
a region (`exact`) is shaped to exactly `rows` by whoever set it, a ceiling
is cropped by whoever imposed it, containers forward less their own rows,
stackers demote a region to a ceiling, and there is no vertical Measurable.

Layout's column split now keeps that promise: each pane is shaped to its
share, so a short pane no longer pulls the panes below it up.

The design document the ticket named is not written: CLAUDE.md forbids a
second description outside docs/, and rich-export-9a1.1 set the precedent
of contract-as-code plus decisions in the sibling tickets (.2, .3, .5).

BREAKING CHANGE: RenderOptions.height is a Height object and maxHeight is
gone. `{ height: n, maxHeight: n }` becomes `{ height: { rows: n, exact: true } }`.

* fix(layout): fill only a region; natural height otherwise, and both splits shape

Review of #162: padding to the 24-row fallback made console.print(layout)
always 24 rows. A layout now fills only an exact region; under a ceiling or
no budget each pane takes its declared size or its content's height, which
deletes the fallback. Rows parse through cellCount (NaN/negative hold none,
Infinity is natural), row splits shape their panes too, and shaping fits the
line count only.

* fix(renderables): containers forward height by the contract

Review of #162: once Layout shapes its panes, a Panel forwarding its region
unchanged let a nested Layout fill it and the crop took the panel's bottom
border. Panel and Padding now inset the budget by their own rows
(insetHeight); Group, Columns and Tree hand each child the rows as a ceiling
(stackedHeight). rich-dash's ClipHeight reserve, which compensated by hand,
is gone.

* fix(renderables): a region's setter shapes it — Panel and Padding too

Escalation review of #162. A Panel handing its content an exact region is
that region's setter, so it now shapes what comes back: its frame stretches
down a pane and a tall body is cropped above the bottom border. The shaping
and the row parse are one pair of helpers in protocol.ts (fitHeight,
regionRows) shared by Layout, Panel and Padding; insetHeight and
stackedHeight parse rows through cellCount. Markdown stacks its blocks.
rich-dash's ClipHeight is deleted as redundant and InjectMaxHeight shapes
the region it sets.
